title: Odd Positions First, Then Even
statement:
You get the head of a singly linked list. Number the nodes by position, starting at 1 for the head. (Positions, not the values stored in the nodes.)

Relink the list so that all nodes at odd positions come first, followed by all nodes at even positions. Inside each group, keep the original order. Return the new head.

Use O(1) extra memory and one pass over the list.

examples.why: Grouping is by position, not by whether the value is odd: 4 is at position 2 and 9 at position 3.
One node is already in order.

hints: Think of it as splitting the list into two lists and then joining them.
Keep two tails: one for the odd-position chain and one for the even-position chain. Each step, the node after the odd tail is the next even node, and the node after that is the next odd node.
Remember where the even chain starts before you begin relinking, and attach it after the last odd node at the end.

explain.intuition:
The list already alternates odd, even, odd, even. So you can peel it into two chains by having each node skip over its neighbour: odd.next = odd.next.next, then the same for even. Both chains keep their original order automatically, because you only ever link forward.

The only thing to remember is the head of the even chain, because once relinking starts nothing points to it. At the end, hang it off the last odd node.
steps: If the list has fewer than 2 nodes, return it as is.
Set odd = head, even = head.next and save evenHead = even.
While even and even.next exist: set odd.next = even.next, move odd forward; set even.next = odd.next, move even forward.
pitfalls: Grouping by the node values instead of positions. [7, 4, 9, 2] keeps 4 in the second half.
Losing the even chain's head, so it cannot be attached at the end.
A loop condition that only checks odd.next: on even-length lists it reads past the end or leaves the last even node pointing back into the odd chain, forming a cycle.

solutions.title: Collect and rebuild
solutions.idea: Copy the nodes into two arrays by position, then relink them odd group first. Easy to get right, but uses O(n) memory.

solutions.title: Two interleaved chains
solutions.idea: Peel the list into an odd chain and an even chain in one pass, then attach the even chain after the odd one.

followups: Split into k groups by position mod k instead of two. What do you need to track?
Undo the operation: given the result and the original length, rebuild the interleaved order in O(1) memory.
